summary.intent: Address an independent review's findings on PR #235 (strict reads / error handling in callisto) before stacking PR 2 on top, then resolve merge conflicts with main and push.
summary.outcome: Review fixes were implemented across graph, model, CLI, and docs; a tautological test was removed and a stale test rewritten; `just ci` passed (exit 0, 92.82% coverage). Fixes were committed and a rebase onto origin/main was started to resolve the docs/errors.md conflict; push and PR 2 rebase not yet done.

repo: `just ci` is the full gate (fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests, coverage); it exits non-zero (e.g. 100) on any failing test and writes a TOTAL coverage line that can be grepped from the log.

Docs are tied to behavior: changes touch ARCHITECTURE.md (atomic_write description), docs/specs/versioning.json (new VER-READ-01 criterion), docs/specs/workspace.json (discovery spec sentence), and docs/errors.md (error code rows like E306–E310).

Dangling .md symlinks (e.g. Emacs lock files `.#x.md`) must be skipped when listing changesets, while other inspection errors (symlink loops, unlistable directories) must still fail and name the entry.

atomic writer policy: skip directory-sync when the directory can't be opened or sync is unsupported (macOS ENOTSUP), but report real errors like EIO; probe_atomic_write runs the same sync check before any effect.
Same-shape strict-read sites exist in matrix.rs (package.json/pyproject.toml reads), napi.rs (manifest read), and init dry-run file listing, which should match what the real run writes.

code.finding: Directory-sync failure handling changed to skip unopenable/unsupported dirs; the test a_directory_sync_failure_is_reported had to be rewritten to the new policy.
Changeset listing now skips dangling symlinks and names the failing entry in errors.

workflow: Use `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only` to preview conflicts without touching a working tree that has CI running.
Avoid modifying files in a worktree while a background `just ci` is running; wait for completion before rebasing.
Remove tautological tests (testing a closure rather than the code under test) instead of keeping false coverage.
Run long CI as a background command with output redirected to a log, then grep for failures and coverage totals.
Fix review findings in the base PR before building stacked PRs on top, then rebase the stack.

friction: `just ci` failed once (exit 100) because a previously valid test pinned old behavior that the review fix intentionally changed.
PR #235 developed merge conflicts in docs/errors.md after #232 and #233 merged to main (E310 row next to E306–E309).
Could not touch the working tree for conflict investigation while CI was running, forcing a wait.
open_items: Push #235 after the rebase onto origin/main completes and checks are re-run (resolve docs/errors.md keeping both sets of rows).
Rebase PR 2 (stacked worktree) onto updated #235; flip old tests pinning the admit-all fallback.
PR 2 must address the review's top finding: membership and root detection still treat an unreadable root manifest as absent.
Deferred: cargo.rs `bin_names` strict read (init scaffolding only), napi.rs 'still on disk' diagnostic.
Deferred to the write-preflight PR: lookups that happen after earlier writes in apply.
